title: NGT vs Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)

blocks.content: The National Green Tribunal was established for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests.

rows: Adjudicates environmental disputes and awards compensation
Monitors pollution levels, sets standards, and provides technical guidance
Passes legally binding judicial orders and penalties
Issues executive directions to industries and SPCBs
Appeals go directly to the Supreme Court of India
Orders can be challenged before appellate authorities or the NGT

items: CPCB was established under the Water Act 1974, but was later entrusted with powers under the Air Act 1981.
India is only the third country in the world (after Australia and New Zealand) to establish a dedicated environmental tribunal like NGT.
Appeals against NGT orders lie directly to the Supreme Court of India within 90 days.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NGT is a specialized judicial body established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, whereas CPCB is a statutory executive body established under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
NGT has powers to adjudicate environmental disputes, enforce legal rights, and award relief and compensation for damages.
CPCB functions as a technical and administrative organization that monitors air and water quality, sets environmental standards, and coordinates State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs).
NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by principles of natural justice.
